Columbia, Missouri · 2026

Background

Engineer. Analyst.
Problem solver.

Joshua Donaldson is a Biological Engineer (Environmental Focus) from the University of Missouri, heading to the University of Leeds as a Marshall Scholar to pursue an MSc in Water, Sanitation, and Health Engineering. He graduated with a 4.0 and minor in Biological Sciences, building technical depth across process scale-up, environmental compliance, circular economy, data engineering, and infrastructure design.

His work sits at the intersection of water, industry, and health. From processing 28,000+ industrial monitoring records at the Environmental Integrity Project to designing a rural water transmission line in Panama, he has worked across technical, policy, and community contexts — translating data into reports, presentations, and decisions that reach real audiences.

He speaks three languages — English, French, and Swahili — and sings as a choral soloist. He sees engineering not as a fixed toolkit but as a way of asking better questions about the world.

Process scale-up · Missouri Water Center

Mold prototyping for ion-imprinted polymers

Prototyped molds for process scale-up of ion-imprinted polymers used for rare earth element recovery from industrial wastewater. The design goal was to prevent fouling and allow backwashing, which meant maximizing sphericity.

Core Expertise

Where I add value.

Industrial Water & Health

Designing and analyzing water systems across industrial and public health contexts — from rural water transmission lines in Panama (break pressure systems, filtration, climate resilience) to rare earth element recovery from industrial wastewater using ion-imprinted polymers at the Missouri Water Center. Grounded in process scale-up, circular economy principles, and the conviction that water infrastructure is as much a public health issue as an engineering one.

Environmental Policy & Compliance

Hands-on work across the full compliance stack: NEPA, CWA, and CAA matrices at Black & Veatch; Phase I & II ESA review for utility-scale infrastructure; wetland permit monitoring and fenceline benzene emissions gap analysis at the Environmental Integrity Project. Built geospatial APIs modeled after EPA EJScreen to bring localized risk data to teams making real regulatory decisions.

Data-Driven Decisions

Applying quantitative methods to problems that matter. Built end-to-end data pipelines processing 28,000+ industrial monitoring records; deployed automated permit-tracking platforms with GitHub Actions; developed environmental justice screening APIs. Also: analyzed 400+ medical records to quantify WIC enrollment impact, and used ArcGIS Max-Ent modeling to predict water quality impairment across Florida. The through-line is turning messy data into something a decision-maker can use.

EPA Noncompliance Dashboard — 130+ Facilities

End-to-end data pipeline processing 28,000+ environmental monitoring records across 130+ industrial facilities, with interactive dashboards and exportable datasets built for a regulatory team making real compliance calls.

Predicting Impaired Water Systems — Florida

ArcGIS Max-Ent model predicting water body impairment from climate variables and hurricane track data — built to support proactive infrastructure planning in a state where water quality failures carry real public health costs.

ArcGISMax-EntClimate Data

Automated Precision Irrigation System

IoT sensor network with Arduino-based controls integrating real-time soil moisture and weather data for precision irrigation scheduling — an early experiment in what smart infrastructure looks like at a small scale.

ArduinoIoTSensor Networks

Urban vs. Rural Waterborne Disease

Used EPA and CDC datasets to analyze water quality disparities and model waterborne disease trends across geographies. The infrastructure gaps driving rural health outcomes are well-documented and largely unaddressed.

REPA DataCDC Data
